Definition: an arrangement, i.e. (concretely) a pile (of loaves)
BiblicalUsage: The word names the rows of the showbread, the twelve loaves set in two rows of six upon the pure table before the LORD, with pure frankincense upon each row. The Levites set the bread in order every Sabbath, and the priests of Abijah's day said they set the shewbread in order upon the pure table and kept the charge of the LORD their God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the rows of bread teach us that God provides for His people continually, and the table before Him is never empty. I hold that the bread set in order every Sabbath is a picture of Christ, the Bread of Life, who is always before the Father on our behalf.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
